smyx-depression-behavioral-markers-analysis 1.0.6

- Updated documentation and removed redundant files (skill-card.md).
- Modified SKILL.md with clarified details and improved instructions.
- Applied adjustments to DAO and utility scripts for enhanced stability.

- Switched user identity parameter handling to be fully automatic and internal—users are no longer prompted for or shown any identity info.
- Softened workflow and documentation: open-id management is now implicit and hidden; skill runs and history queries both operate without user input for identity.
- Updated and streamlined documentation to clarify data privacy, workflow, and requirements; removed explicit open-id acquisition steps from user-facing instructions.
- Adjusted scripts, config, and documentation to align with new internal-only handling of user identity, improving user privacy and experience.
- Removed user-facing files related to manual identity handling.
- General UI, UX, and codebase cleanup for better maintainability and clarity.

smyx-depression-behavioral-markers-analysis v1.0.0

- Initial release focused on non-clinical, AI-powered behavioral observation for detecting potential depressive tendencies in elderly or solo-living individuals using fixed bedroom and dining area cameras.
- Monitors multi-day patterns in lying-in-bed duration (>20 hours/day) and sharp decreases in eating frequency/duration (eating-action count <50% of personal baseline).
- Generates daily behavior summaries and pushes alerts if abnormal patterns persist beyond a customizable threshold (e.g., 3 days).
- Strict privacy, user identification, and data-fetch safeguards: requires open-id before analysis or historical report queries, with a defined retrieval flow.
- Can be integrated into home-care cameras or health-management platforms to support remote mental-health monitoring and timely intervention.
- Provides structured observation reports and friendly reminders; not a medical diagnostic tool.
